editorial.headline: Wholesale Sweets: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity spans sugar, chocolate, confectionery and sweetener preparations—open nationally to full foreign ownership, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
The activity covers wholesale trade in sugar, chocolate, confectionery and sweetener preparations. Its focus is the commercial movement of these goods at wholesale level: a clear category for businesses whose work centres on supplying that range of products. The code is broad in product scope, yet its registration setting must be read with equal care, particularly where foreign investment and location intersect.

The stated scale range is equally broad. Micro, small, medium and large enterprises are all included, placing the activity within the code’s declared reach at every listed business scale. That matters because scale is not a decorative label here: it becomes central to the Bali outcome. A business may fit the activity by the goods it trades and by the scale at which it operates, while still facing a different registration result according to the jurisdiction in which it proposes to establish itself.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity. That is the national position recorded under the cited presidential regulations, and it should be understood precisely as that: a national ownership setting. It does not, by itself, determine whether a PMA company can be registered in every province.

In Bali, the answer changes decisively. A foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA business in Bali today. The record identifies the large-scale OSS risk classification as Low or Medium-Low across every scope, which brings the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for those risk levels. The cited moratorium date is May 13, 2026. There is no Bali-specific ownership percentage in the record to soften or qualify this result. For this code, national openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remain real facts—but they do not overcome Bali’s registration block.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not overcome Bali’s registration block.
